sentence: NorthStar Freight Pvt. Ltd. Business Plan 2026-2029 This document is a fictional sample plan created for practicing text extraction and assumption detection.
All names and numbers are invented.
NorthStar Freight is a regional road-freight company operating 48 trucks across Gujarat and Maharashtra.
In 2025 the company earned revenue of Rs. 42.5 crore and an operating margin of 9.2%.
The management plans to expand the fleet to 90 trucks by the end of 2028.
The plan rests on a small number of key assumptions.
We assume that the average diesel price will stay at or below Rs. 92 per litre throughout the plan period.
We expect the global crude oil price to remain between USD 65 and USD 80 per barrel.
We also assume that freight demand in our corridors will grow by 8% per year.
If these assumptions hold, revenue is projected to reach Rs. 96 crore by 2029.
The company will seek Rs. 15 crore in funding to buy 30 new trucks and two warehouse sites.
Our largest customers are three FMCG distributors who together contribute 55% of revenue.
The head office is located in Ahmedabad.
Fuel accounts for roughly 38% of our operating cost, so fuel price is the single most important cost driver.
Management believes that crude oil will trade near USD 72 per barrel on average during 2026.
Prices above USD 90 per barrel would reduce the operating margin by about 3 percentage points.
Driver wages are expected to rise by 6% per year.
Tyre and maintenance costs are assumed to increase by 4% per year.
The company does not currently hedge fuel costs.
The Indian road-freight market is projected to grow at around 7% annually over the next five years.
We assume our own volumes will grow slightly faster than the market because of two new warehouse-linked contracts.
Customer churn is assumed to stay below 5% per year.
Competition in the region is fragmented, with more than 200 small operators.
No single competitor holds more than 4% market share.
The table below summarises the base-case projections.
All figures are in Rs. crore unless stated otherwise.
Revenue growth in the base case is driven by the 8% annual demand growth assumption and by the fleet expansion.
We assume an average fleet utilisation of 82% in every year.
Freight rates are expected to rise by 5% per year, in line with inflation.
The interest rate on the proposed term loan is assumed to be 10.5%, and we do not expect it to change by more than 1 percentage point during the loan period.
The rupee is assumed to trade at about Rs. 84 per US dollar.
The main risk to the plan is a sustained rise in fuel prices.
In a downside scenario where crude oil averages USD 95 per barrel, we estimate that the 2027 operating margin would fall from 10.9% to about 7%.
A second risk is the loss of one of the three anchor customers.
The board reviews the plan every six months.
Management will revisit the funding request if diesel prices exceed Rs. 100 per litre for more than one quarter.
The company expects regulatory changes on emission norms to have only a minor impact before 2028.
The founders hold 70% of the equity.
Contact details for investors are available on request.
